articles.title: Gerwyn Price sets up Grand Slam final showdown with Gian van Veen with Michael van Gerwen defeated in semis
articles.summary: Gerwyn Price beat Kevin Doets and Gian van Veen beat Michael van gerwen to make it into the Grand Slam of Darts final; watch the final of the Grand Slam of Darts from 7.30pm live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Gerwyn Price came up with a 16-13 win over Kevin Doets in the semi-finals on Sunday afternoon, while Van Veen defeated Michael van Gerwen 16-11.

Price is targeting a fourth Grand Slam title, adding to his triumphs in 2018, 2019 and 2021.

There is also a big move in the rankings on the line for the Welshman as, if he wins, he will become world No 3, dropping Luke Humphries to world No 4.

Meanwhile, provisional world No 2 Van Veen is searching for his maiden Grand Slam title.

Price came through a real battle to make it into another final. He is aiming to maintain his perfect finals record in Wolverhampton and believes that over the majors in 2026, he has been the most consistent performer.

"I am into another final and I am not playing great," Price told Sky Sports . "I have played okay in patches this tournament. I am in another final and I am happy.

"I have probably been the most consistent player this season as far as majors are concerned.

"I obviously want to win this and there are some big ranking points at stake but I am just happy to get to another final.

"I care - there is £100,000 at stake and if I don't care about that there is something wrong - but if I lose it is another final.

"It is not about trophies, it is about earning a living for my family.

"I am just a rugby player pinching a living!"

It was a tight opening session between the pair from which Price took a 3-2 lead, increasing that to 4-2 with his fourth leg in a row.

Doets battled back but a brilliant 137 checkout and then break of throw from the Welshman put him 6-4 ahead.

From there, Price went on a rampage. He reeled off six legs in a row to get to double figures. Doets stopped the rot with a break of throw but the 10-4 scoreline showed how everything was going the Welshman's way.

Despite Price's momentum, Doets dug deep and won five on the next six legs to move the score to 11-9 and eventually 14-12.

However, the key moment came in the 27th leg when Doets missed two chances to break Price's throw and instead of bringing the score to 14-13, he went 15-12 behind.

That gave Price enough breathing space to wait for his throw, then take out a big 171 to leave 94 which he checked out on tops for a 12-darter.

"Price had control and did things at the right times.

"When he seems to have the most trouble in matches is when he has a big lead. Perhaps his focus gets away from a bit.

"Ultimately, the real clutch darts were Price's and now you have to say he is the favourite in the final."

It was expected to be a close contest between the two Dutch darting stars and early on it was just that with Van Gerwen and Van Veen matching each other in every department.

That saw the game levelled at 5-5 and it was clear someone was going to have to take control.

However, it was not necessarily that Van Veen took control. Some disastrous doubling for both players, but in particular Van Gerwen, proved to be the key factor.

As Van Veen improved, Van Gerwen continued to mess around on the outer ring which allowed his opponent to go from 7-6 down to 10-7 ahead.

Although Van Gerwen tried to get himself back into the contest, a burst of four legs in a row moved Van Veen one leg away from the Grand Slam final, a massive 124 checkout on the bullseye getting him there.

Van Gerwen did hold his throw but it was purely a consolation as the Dutch No 1 pinned 107 on D16 for his first Grand Slam final.

Watch the final of the Grand Slam of Darts live on Sky Sports Main Event from 7.30pm.

articles.title: 'Los Gallos' siguen imparables: ¡logran en Dubai su noveno podio de la temporada de SailGP!
articles.standfirst: El equipo español acaba tercero y llega lanzado a la Gran Final en Abu Dabi del próximo fin de semana. Peleará por su segundo título tras el de 2024
articles.summary: El equipo español acaba tercero y llega lanzado a la Gran Final en Abu Dabi del próximo fin de semana. Peleará por su segundo título tras el de 2024
articles.body: A sólo una semana de que se celebre la Gran Final (29 de noviembre) de la sexta temporada de SailGP en Abu Dabi, el equipo español presentó su candidatura al título en el Gran Premio de Dubai. En las aguas de Mina Rashid acabó tercero y sumó su noveno podio de la temporada (3 victorias, 2 segundos y 4 terceros). 'Los Gallos' están protagonizando la mejor temporada de su historia con 9 podios de 11 y teniendo en cuenta que no compitió en dos (Perth y Nueva York) por problemas técnicos del F50. Se mantienen firmes en el segundo puesto del Rolex SailGP Championship. Diego Botín, Florian Trittel, Joel Rodríguez, Nicole Van der Velden, Joan Cardona y Bernardo Freitas quieren coser la segunda Copa en su camiseta. Este domingo salieron al agua como líderes del Grupo A con 8 puntos, uno de ventaja sobre Estados Unidos y dos respecto a Alemania y Nueva Zelanda. 'Los Gallos', que el sábado habían acabado segundos las dos mangas disputadas, no se jugaban nada porque ya tenían el billete sellado para la Gran Final de Abu Dabi desde hace dos meses, cuando ganaron en Ginebra, pero su gen competitivo no les permite relajarse y salieron a por todas. En las dos mangas de hoy, España acabó tercera. En la primera, el equipo español maniobró 90 grados hacia la izquierda y salió por detrás de la flota. Un truco que le valió para colocarse cuarto al paso de la primera boya. Superaron a los neozelandeses en el tramo contrario al viento y a punto estuvieron de sobrepasar a Canadá en la recta final. Y en la segunda, repitieron puesto. Su regularidad le sirvió para ser primera de grupo y pasar a la final junto a los neozelandeses, liderados por Peter Burling. 'Los Gallos' y los Black Foils esperaban para conocer a sus rivales del Grupo B, que acabarían siendo los BONDS Fying Roos australianos y el Artemis sueco. En la final, los Black Foils demostraron que Dubai se les da bien y sumaron su tercera victoria allí. Es la primera de la tripulación de Peter Burling esta complicada temporada, en la que no han podido competir con normalidad tras la colisión con Francia en Auckland. La victoria les otorga, además, 400.000 dólares. Por detrás acabó la Australia de Tom Slingsby, líder indiscutible esta temporada en la que ha ganado cinco Grandes Premios. España, que al igual que Artemis fue penalizada por salir antes de tiempo (un fuera de línea), acabó tercera. “Ha sido un fin de semana muy sólido. Hemos estado delante en todas las carreras, excepto en la final, donde un fallo del software nos ha penalizado. Hemos tenido que fijarnos en los otros tres barcos, y por eso nos hemos adelantado un poco. En cualquier caso, hemos cogido confianza para el domingo que viene”, comentó Diego Botín, piloto del equipo español, al término del evento. La flota de SailGP pondrá rumbo ahora a Abu Dabi, donde el próximo fin de semana se celebrará el último Gran Premio de la temporada (28 y 29) y el domingo, los tres mejores barcos de la temporada, lucharán por el título de campeones y los 2 millones de dólares de premio. Australia y España ya tienen su clasificación asegurada desde hace un par de meses. El Artemis sueco (66 puntos) y el equipo estadounidense (59) mantendrán la lucha por la tercera plaza hasta el final. Emirates Gran Bretaña, campeón en 2025, se ha quedado sin opciones de revalidar el título. Australia partirá con el cartel de favorita tras sus coronas de (2019, 2022 y 2023, pero esta temporada el equipo español ya ha ganado tres finales y no le tiene miedo.

articles.title: Max Verstappen Mocks George Russell in Viral Video After Winning F1 Las Vegas GP Race
articles.summary: The 2026 Formula One championship race might be over, but Max Verstappen still has plenty to drive for, namely bragging rights over George Russell.
articles.body:
The 2026 Formula One championship race might be over, but Max Verstappen still has plenty to drive for, namely bragging rights over George Russell.

Verstappen captured the checkered flag in the Las Vegas Grand Prix on Saturday, while Russell tumbled from third to ninth with two laps remaining.

Speaking to reporters after the race, Verstappen twisted the knife a bit by saying Russell "is so far below my level." The four-time F1 champion also reveled in peeking at his rearview mirror and seeing Russell in the wall:

Needless to say, the bad blood between Verstappen and Russell goes beyond your typical rivalry between two drivers who each have championship aspirations.

Verstappen's newest volley follows critical remarks from Russell after qualifying in Las Vegas. Russell took exception to Verstappen's aggressive driving during the final practice and said as much publicly.

"There's nothing in the rules to say you cannot overtake someone who is starting their lap but when you do this you are screwing this person over and he does this week-in, week-out with many drivers and everybody accepts it," Russell said to Sky Italia (via the Guardian 's Giles Richards ). "I'm not just going to accept somebody to screw me over like this, and walk around like they're bigger and better than everyone else. Somebody has got to stand up to that guy."

It's little surprise that Verstappen savored Saturday's win so much after the verbal back-and-forth.

On the whole, finishing a distant runner-up to Kimi Antonelli will likely mean the 2026 season is a disappointment to the Dutchman. He'll take some satisfaction from looking down on Russell in the standings.

articles.title: Gukesh vs Sindarov press conference: Who said what before World Chess Championship 2026
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Ahead of Game 1 of the 2026 World Chess Championship on November 24 at the Fondation Martin Bodmer in Cologny, Geneva, defending champion
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Ahead of Game 1 of the 2026 World Chess Championship on November 24 at the Fondation Martin Bodmer in Cologny, Geneva, defending champion Dommaraju Gukesh and challenger Javokhir Sindarov shared their thoughts on preparation, expectations, and facing each other in the youngest world title match in chess history.Here is what both players said during the opening press conference.GukeshOn defending the world title:"Well, I don't think I'm here to defend anything. I'm here to win it all over again, I think. So that's the mindset I'm in."On returning to a World Championship match after 2024:"Compared to the last time, it feels like I'm more experienced coming into the match, but whatever has happened till now just gets erased when we sit at the table for Game 1. It's a completely different match, completely different opponent, different place. So I'm not really thinking about other things, just giving my best for these 14 games."On how preparation differs from his first title match:"I think the preparation differs from match to match. Also, in 2024, I was playing a lot more than I did this year. Sometimes it just feels like hard work. When you do certain kinds of work, sometimes it feels like fun and creativity flowing around. Working with the team that I enjoy being around is one of the most important things for me. Even when the work is exhausting or stressful, you're still surrounded by people who you like being around, and that gives you a lot of strength."On the best part of his training camps:"I feel like the best part about this whole World Championship journey is the training camps. It's so much fun, so much good work, so much laughing, so many jokes. With Gaju [Grzegorz Gajewski], I share a very close personal bond, and the training camps are probably the things that I will most remember after the match."On Javokhir Sindarov’s form and playing style:"Sindarov has just been in very consistent and very good form and is surely one of the very top players at the very top of his game. When you play a World Championship, it's very nice that it's just one opponent so you can put full attention on that one specific player. There's a lot of analyzing your opponent going on, though only to an extent because Sindarov is very universal. He can play any position at a decent level. It's just you sharpening your skills and understanding your opponent to a good degree."On Sindarov playing a heavy tournament schedule in 2026:"Not really [surprised]. Me and my team kind of expected that he'll play more than me. We had decided to slow down the tournaments quite a bit this year. This is kind of the first year that he has been playing at the very elite, and we just thought it made sense that he'll make use of the good momentum and get more experience against the top guys."On inspecting the playing hall at Fondation Martin Bodmer:"It was basically checking whether I'd be able to feel comfortable for four or five hours every day. I checked the chairs, the lighting, the floors—different kinds of things that can bother you during a game. I was happy with pretty much everything. About the books, I just saw there were a lot of books. I didn't really bother to check what books they are, but I don't think I'll be reading in between the games."On advice from his inner circle:"In difficult moments, somebody says, 'Just go there and express yourself. Doesn't matter whatever happens, we are there for you.' And one thing that has stayed with me over the last few months is somebody telling me, 'Remember who you are.' In this match, I will remember that."On food and staying balanced during the match:"I generally prefer food that I'm comfortable with. Usually I eat a lot of Indian food, and some people in Geneva have been very kind to prepare food for me. So I'm getting home-cooked Indian food, which I'm very comfortable with, and I'm really grateful for it."Javokhir SindarovOn his chances of winning the championship:"I think the chances are 50-50. I don't want to say anything because the match will be very tough. So I think it's normal to give 50-50 because it's a hard match, and in 14 games everything can happen."On reaching his first World Championship match:"It passed very fast. I was traveling a lot and played many tournaments. Today I'm here, I'm very happy to fight for this crown, and I'll try to enjoy the match. I know it will be very hard. It's my first experience, and we'll see, but anyway, I'm happy because many chess players play chess their whole life and don't get a chance to play for this."On Gukesh’s recent form and strengths:"Gukesh's performance in 2024 is something fantastic. We all know how well he played. Of course, if you look at last year, he was unlucky. But still, this year I played against him in Tata Steel and I felt how strong he really is. Sometimes you have some bad periods, but I think it doesn't mean a lot because we also saw Ding in 2024, he played very bad tournaments, but still in a match he played well. I learned from his games a lot. He has a very good strength in typical positions, his calculation is very good, and Gukesh can fight until the end."On why he played so many tournaments before Geneva:"First, I had an invitation for the Grand Chess Tour before I won the Candidates, and when you get the chance to play such a strong tournament, you immediately agree to play. My goal, even after I won the Candidates, was to have more experience because I hadn't played that many strong tournaments in my career. From this year, I really started playing strong tournaments like Tata Steel. That's why I chose to play many tournaments, and I'm happy with my decision."On preparing for a 14-game match for the first time:"The most different part of preparation compared to Swiss tournaments or small mini-matches is the openings—you need to work really a lot. I was thinking six months was enough time, but maybe even these six months are not enough to prepare for such a hard tournament. When someone told me it takes three or four months to prep for a World Championship match, I never believed that could be normal, but now I understand how preparation goes. It was really hard, but exciting."On revealing members of his coaching team:"In my team here, everyone knows Roman [Vidonyak], Muhiddin [Madaminov] is also here, and Nikita Vitiugov is helping me here."On playing in a venue without a glass booth or surrounding boards:"It's my first time when there is nobody playing around us, only we are playing, and it can be boring sometimes because you don't know whom to watch! Even in other tournaments when I played, there was always someone whom I watched. In general, the playing hall is really very beautiful. I was thinking I would play in a box, so it looks very fine, and I hope for a great match."On staying physically and mentally sharp and playing padel:"After Cyprus, I started playing padel and started loving this sport, and I have played a lot in my camps too. I think you also have to do some physical things. Because I'm young, I think it won't be very hard physically, but mentally it's important, and I work on that with my coaches."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Luke Littler values legacy and darts titles over money as he launches initiative to help reduce youth unemployment
articles.summary: Luke Littler and The Kings Trust join forces to help young people find employment through practical job skills and work experience; Littler to defend World Darts Championship title live on Sky Sports from December 11 after second-round exit at Grand Slam of Darts
articles.body:
Two-time world champion Littler, 19, and The Kings Trust have established the 'Luke Littler Opportunity Fund', which aims to assist young people in finding employment through practical job skills and work experience.

The world No 1, who will look for a hat-trick of titles at Alexandra Palace live on Sky Sports from December 11, told the Big Issue after becoming its youngest guest editor: "I just love what I do. Once that love for the game goes, then I'll obviously stop, whenever that is.

"It's just the drive, the momentum you get when I'm going on stage, knowing that if I hit this double, you're into the final or I'm world champion.

"Many people are like, 'oh, money's got to his head', but it's never been about the money. I've never grown up with a lot of money, so now I've got it, I'm not going to go and use it all.

"I want titles and legacy in the game of darts."

On his new initiative to help reduce youth unemployment, Littler, who has become an ambassador for The King's Trust, added: "Help is needed all across the country. I'd like to focus on the north because I've seen many people struggling.

"The King's Trust gives opportunities to people, whether it's to build a bit of confidence or to find their feet and find a job.

"I just want to get out there, be an ambassador and help people out. Darts has given me a path in life and opened up so many amazing opportunities for me at a young age.

"Not everyone gets the same start and I want this fund to be something we can build over the coming years and hopefully get lots of people behind it so we can make a real difference to young people across the north west."

Littler's friends also contributed to the Big Issue, including Manchester United and England footballer Ella Toone and fellow darts player Beau Greaves.

Littler said: "I've really enjoyed guest editing and getting some familiar faces involved to share their own stories.

"Hopefully, together we can get more people talking about the importance of giving young people opportunities, whatever their background."

articles.title: Inside Alexander Zverev and Brenda Patea’s latest legal dispute over his 2026 French Open interview
articles.summary: Alexander Zverev has been served with a fresh lawsuit from his former partner Brenda Patea over comments he made about their 2024 court case.
articles.body: Alexander Zverev has been served with a fresh lawsuit from his former partner Brenda Patea over comments he made about their 2024 court case. The German tennis star received the legal papers on November 18 while competing at the ATP Finals in Turin. Patea, who shares a daughter with Zverev, claims he broke their private agreement by saying his innocence had been proven. Her lawyer wants the court to stop him from repeating those remarks and is also seeking financial damages.Brenda Patea Takes Legal Action Against Alexander Zverev Over His French Open InterviewThe new legal dispute comes from an interview Zverev gave to French sports newspaper L'Equipe after winning his first French Open title in June 2026. During the conversation, he was asked about the reaction from journalists who had covered his first Grand Slam victory despite the earlier allegations against him.Zverev did not appear pleased with the question. He responded by saying that the accusations had been proven false and asked the interviewer whether they knew that his innocence had been proven.However, Patea's lawyer Michael Scheele believes this was an incorrect account of what happened in court. He told the Daily Mail Sport that both sides had agreed not to discuss the case publicly after reaching an agreement in 2024.According to Scheele, Patea first tried to resolve the matter without taking further legal action. Her legal team sent letters asking Zverev not to repeat his comments. However, they received no response. Patea then filed a civil claim in Berlin on September 18.Scheele also explained why his client had initially taken a careful approach. Patea did not want to create further problems because she and Zverev share a daughter. She also depends on the financial support he provides for their child.The lawyer said Patea was upset after reading Zverev's comments in the media. He believes the remarks led to more criticism of his client and affected her public image and work as an influencer.Patea is now seeking an order that would prevent Zverev from making similar statements again. Her legal team has also asked for a penalty of up to €250,000 each time he breaks the proposed order.Alexander Zverev's 2024 Court Case Ended Without a VerdictThe latest lawsuit is connected to allegations Patea made against Zverev over an incident in May 2020. She accused him of pushing her against a wall and choking her during an argument in Berlin. Zverev has repeatedly denied the allegations.The case reached court in Germany in 2024. However, the proceedings ended after both sides agreed to a settlement. Zverev agreed to pay €150,000 to the state and €50,000 to a charity.Importantly, the court did not find him guilty or declare him innocent. The case was closed without a verdict, and the settlement did not amount to an admission of guilt.Patea's lawyer has also said that his client did not receive any personal compensation from Zverev as part of that agreement. He believes the public claim that Zverev's innocence was proven has added to the criticism she has faced.Meanwhile, Zverev's legal team has made its position clear. His lawyers, Christian Schertz and Anna Sophie Heuchemer, confirmed that they had received the lawsuit on November 18. They said their client would defend himself against the claims.The lawyers also argued that if Zverev made the comments as reported, they could be considered a protected expression of opinion under the German Constitution. They denied that he had broken any contractual agreement.Zverev has not personally commented on the new lawsuit. The legal dispute is now separate from the criminal case that ended in 2024, and the court has yet to decide on Patea's latest claims.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Nacional estalla contra Jhon Ospina y exige audios del VAR tras roja a Felipe Marín
articles.standfirst: El duro reclamo de Nacional a Jhon Ospina tras la roja a Felipe Marín y su historial de expulsiones
articles.summary: El duro reclamo de Nacional a Jhon Ospina tras la roja a Felipe Marín y su historial de expulsiones
articles.body: El empate 0-0 entre Once Caldas y Atlético Nacional en el estadio Palogrande de Manizales, correspondiente a la primera fecha de los cuadrangulares semifinales de la Liga BetPlay Dimayor 2026-II (disputado el sábado 21 de noviembre de 2026), dejó como principal foco de discusión el arbitraje de Jhon Alexander Ospina y la tarjeta roja directa mostrada al volante verdolaga Felipe Marín antes del descanso. Este domingo 22 de noviembre, Atlético Nacional emitió un pronunciamiento público en el que calificó como "inexplicable" la expulsión de Marín, solicitó formalmente a la Federación Colombiana de Fútbol y a la Comisión Arbitral Nacional la revisión de la jugada y la publicación de los audios del VAR, y expuso datos estadísticos sobre el historial del juez vallecaucano en partidos del conjunto antioqueño. Cerca del final de la primera mitad (alrededor del minuto 39-40), en una acción dividida en el mediocampo, Felipe Marín intentó disputar y recuperar el balón, pero terminó impactando en la zona proximal a la tibia de un rival. El árbitro central Jhon Ospina sancionó la acción con tarjeta roja directa. La jugada fue sometida a revisión del VAR, pero la decisión inicial se mantuvo en el campo, obligando a Atlético Nacional a disputar más de la mitad del compromiso con diez futbolistas en un escenario complejo y ante un rival con el que venía de encadenar duelos de máxima tensión. Pese a jugar en inferioridad numérica durante gran parte del encuentro, el equipo dirigido en campo sostuvo el empate sin goles y sumó un punto como visitante en el arranque del cuadrangular. Sin embargo, para la dirigencia y el entorno verdolaga, la expulsión alteró el desarrollo táctico del partido y dejó un malestar profundo por el criterio aplicado tanto en la cancha como desde la cabina de videoarbitraje. En su comunicado, Atlético Nacional aclaró que mantiene el respeto por la labor de los árbitros y reconoció que el error forma parte del juego, pero insistió en que existen límites cuando una acción es revisada por el VAR y aun así se ratifica una determinación que consideran injustificada. Los puntos centrales del reclamo institucional son: Publicación de los audios del VAR: Pedir transparencia total sobre la conversación y el análisis técnico entre el árbitro central y el equipo VAR en las jugadas determinantes del compromiso en Manizales. Revisión de la expulsión: Solicitar a la FCF y a la Comisión Arbitral Nacional que evalúen lo ocurrido con Felipe Marín antes de que avancen las siguientes jornadas de los cuadrangulares semifinales. Criterios claros en las designaciones: Exigir que las asignaciones arbitrales para la definición del campeonato respondan a parámetros técnicos verificables y ofrezcan garantías para todos los clubes. Más allá de la acción puntual en Palogrande, el comunicado de Atlético Nacional puso el foco en los antecedentes de Jhon Ospina dirigiendo al cuadro verdolaga, presentando cifras para respaldar su inconformidad: Partidos dirigidos por Jhon Ospina a Nacional: 26 encuentros Tarjetas rojas mostradas por Ospina a Nacional: 9 expulsiones Frecuencia comparada: +78 % frente a otros árbitros Registro general de Nacional (desde enero de 2021): 76 rojas en 383 partidos Para Atlético Nacional, esta diferencia estadística alimenta la sensación de desventaja cuando el juez vallecaucano es designado para sus compromisos, especialmente en instancias decisivas del semestre.

articles.title: F1 set to reduce customer teams as key 2030 details emerge
articles.summary: As part of its 2030 plan to V8 power units, Formula 1 power unit manufacturers are set to only supply two teams, prompting political intrigue over the future...
articles.body:
F1 is planning a shift to just two power unit supplies per manufacturer in 2030, Motorsport.com has learned, raising questions over the status of Mercedes' three current customers.

Over the Las Vegas weekend the FIA announced there was unanimous support to bring the next generation of power unit regulations forward to 2030. That includes a move to 2.1-litre V8 engines, including a turbocharger, a maximum of 200 kilowatts of electric power and the use of sustainable fuels.

That move satisfies the demand for cheaper and less complex engines, which FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem and F1 chief Stefano Domenicali had been pursuing in unison. Meanwhile, adding a turbo was a key requirement for the likes of Audi and also ensures engine noise remains at a suitable level for some of F1's urban venues.

What was also part of a wide-ranging document the FIA produced on the 2030 framework, but wasn't part of the public announcement, is an agreement between the six 2030 power unit manufacturers to supply just two teams each. This also includes their works team, leaving just one single engine supply available for external customer teams.

Motorsport.com understands that one aim of the move is to reduce the political influence of manufacturers supplying a large share of the grid, in this case Mercedes and Ferrari , while the manufacturers in question had also been willing to downsize as supplying F1 engines is a loss making operation, with supplies capped at just $18m per season.

Ferrari is currently supplying the works team, Haas and Cadillac, but the latter will be moving to in-house engines from 2030, meaning the question of Ferrari's supply is solving itself. Red Bull Powertrains will also be taking care of two teams, Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls , while at present Audi, Aston Martin partner Honda and Cadillac's shareholder General Motors will all have their own works teams as their one and only confirmed customer.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Lando Norris, McLaren

That leaves the question of what will happen to Mercedes and the customers of Mercedes High Performance Powertrains. Alongside the works team in Brackley, the Brixworth operation is currently supplying McLaren , Williams as well as Alpine , whose parent company Renault recently abandoned and sold its in-house engine operation.

Per the 2030 framework, two of those three teams would be looking for a new engine supply if the FIA World Motor Sport Council approves the proposal in Shanghai next month. That seismic shift will set up months of political intrigue in the F1 paddock as teams scramble to secure what has been F1's most reliable and performant power unit supplier ever since F1 moved to hybrid engines in 2014, or conclude deals with currently less desirable options.

Motorsport.com understands that both McLaren and Williams are fancying their chances of remaining with Mercedes. And while McLaren at least explored the idea of becoming its own power unit manufacturer when a move to a cheaper formula would make that more feasible than it is now, CEO Zak Brown indicated that ship has sailed for 2030 as he aims to remain a Mercedes customer.

"It's something we've looked at in the past, but we're very happy with HPP," Brown said in Las Vegas on Thursday. "I think we've proven that we can win championships with them, so we don't have any intention to have anything in the back of our car other than a Mercedes."

Zak Brown on the idea of McLaren building its own engines:

Mercedes' intentions about what its ideal customer team would look like are less clear right now. Having been beaten by McLaren in 2024 and 2025, CEO Toto Wolff maintained that a win for a customer is still a feather in the cap for HPP and the Mercedes brand as a whole, while a strong customer team also provides a valuable chassis benchmark for the works operation.

And while Brown hailed HPP as an "awesome partner", it's no secret that the relationship between HPP and McLaren has at least come under some strain at the start of this year amid a knowledge gap between the works team and its customer over how to exploit and deploy the complex new power units.

Whether Mercedes will continue to lease engines to its most formidable rival or whether a deal with a midfield team is the preferred option will likely become the subject of plenty of intrigue in the coming months.

What is certain is that the FIA's proposed third-party engine plan is now dead in the water. With F1 power units becoming less complex and expensive in 2030, FIA president Ben Sulayem had floated the idea of sourcing a supply of off-the-shelf, white label engines to further alleviate concerns over team independence.

However, that plan never seemed economically viable for any prospective engine builder, and with all six PUMs at the table now unanimously agreeing to 2030's key infrastructure, a cap of two supplies would mean there are at least 12 power unit supplies available for 11 teams.

The FIA did include a safety net in case one of the six manufacturers decides to drop out, adding a clause under which a departing manufacturer's F1 power unit intellectual property would transfer to the FIA, which could then assign it to a new manufacturer coming in.

As is the case today, there will also be an "obligation to supply", meaning the FIA could force one of the manufacturers to supply an additional, third team with an engine if that outfit can't arrange a deal to find one, which may well end up becoming a key clause.

FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem and F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali have long been in agreement over the future direction of F1's power units.

What has also been agreed is the basis for the power unit cost cap for the 2030-2034 period. The cap will remain at today's figure of $190m for 2030 before falling by $7.5m per year, ending at $160m for the 2034 season.

That sliding scale helps manufacturers with the initial development cost of the new power units. A development freeze of the current engines from 2028, as well as a ban on V8 dyno testing until the summer of that year, is expected to help F1's current manufacturers manage their resources between the two projects. Existing manufacturers will also receive more cost-cap headroom than newcomer General Motors, which can now abandon its V6 plans and just focus on the V8 program in Charlotte. GM is understood to be signing up to a budget cap of $170m for the first couple of years.

There are still several important topics to be fleshed out further by the manufacturers, such as the exact nature of the electric push-to-pass system as it would need to work in conjunction with the chassis design to promote close racing.

But by defining the overarching framework and key engine architecture, which will be rubber stamped by the FIA World Motor Sport Council, both the manufacturers and the FIA can now get to work on the next rules cycle on a reasonable timeline.

That should help the governing body come up with chassis regulations which are tuned to work well with the new power units and deliver a more pure and exciting set of rules, without facing the prospect of having to adapt to late U-turns by OEMs, which led to 2026's compromised and criticised formula to begin with.

articles.title: Steelers' DK Metcalf ejected for unsportsmanlike conduct vs. the Eagles
articles.summary: PHILADELPHIA (AP) — Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf was ejected for unsportsmanlike conduct in the third quarter of Sunday's game at Philadelphi...
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA (AP) — Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf was ejected for unsportsmanlike conduct in the third quarter of Sunday's game at Philadelphia.

Metcalf was twice involved in fights against the Eagles.

He was flagged for unnecessary roughness earlier in the game after he went after cornerback Cooper DeJean. Metcalf appeared to poke DeJean in the eyes in the second scuffle and was flagged for unsportsmanlike conduct and was tossed.

Metcalf finished with one catch for two yards, two personal fouls and an ejection. He was ejected for the third time in his career.

The NFL suspended Metcalf for two games last season following an in-game altercation between Metcalf and a fan during the team's victory over Detroit.

articles.title: Cunningham has double-double as No. 6 Texas women lead throughout 75-61 over No. 19 Ohio State
articles.summary: FORT WORTH, Texas (AP) — Breya Cunningham had 24 points and 13 rebounds as No. 6 Texas never trailed in a 75-61 win over No.
articles.body:
FORT WORTH, Texas (AP) — Breya Cunningham had 24 points and 13 rebounds as No. 6 Texas never trailed in a 75-61 win over No. 19 Ohio State on Sunday, when the Longhorns played in the same arena where they clinched their NCAA Final Four berth last season.

Jayda Clark had 15 points and five assists for the Longhorns (6-0) to go along with Cunningham's 11th career double-double.

Two-time first-team AP All-America forward Madison Booker finished with 12 points and nine rebounds for Texas after missing her first eight shots, and not scoring until a fastbreak layup off an Ohio State turnover with 7:15 left in the third quarter. Her seven turnovers were one short of her career high set as a freshman against West Virginia.

Texas led 53-43 going into the fourth quarter before Cunningham's three-point play opened a run of 16 points in a row in less than 2 1/2 minutes for the Longhorns. Ohio State scored the last 13 points after most starters were out of the game.

Jaloni Cambridge, who had a 3-pointer at the end of the third quarter for Ohio State (5-2), finished with 27 points. The Buckeyes were coming off a home win over No. 19 Mississippi when Cambridge also had 27 points.

The Longhorns were also at Ariat Arena in downtown Fort Worth last March, when the building was known as Dickies Arena and they beat Kentucky in a Sweet 16 matchup before a 77-41 rout over Michigan to advance to their second consecutive Final Four.

They also played a neutral-site game there last December, when Booker had 27 points and eight rebounds in an 89-54 win over then-No. 13 Baylor .

Ohio State plays VCU on Saturday in Richmond, Va.

Texas hosts Southeastern Louisiana on Wednesday.

articles.title: Los detalles de la oferta de Win Sports para quedarse con los derechos del fútbol colombiano
articles.standfirst: Win Sports lanza millonaria oferta por los derechos del fútbol colombiano: lo que se sabe
articles.summary: Win Sports lanza millonaria oferta por los derechos del fútbol colombiano: lo que se sabe
articles.body: El futuro audiovisual del Fútbol Profesional Colombiano atraviesa su momento más decisivo de cara a 2027. Tras semanas de rumores, presiones comerciales y versiones cruzadas en los medios, Win Sports radicó formalmente ante la Dimayor una contraoferta millonaria para conservar los derechos de transmisión de los torneos del balompié nacional, superando el umbral de los 90 millones de dólares anuales que había puesto sobre la mesa la competencia. La definición final quedó en manos de la Asamblea General de la Dimayor, convocada para el miércoles 25 de noviembre de 2026 en Bogotá, donde los 36 clubes afiliados analizarán y votarán las propuestas en disputa para establecer quién llevará las emociones de la Liga, el Torneo, la Copa, la Superliga y el fútbol femenino a partir del próximo año. La disputa cambió de escala cuando se conoció la oferta atribuida al consorcio Go Sports Media, encabezado por el empresario Mauricio Correa, una propuesta cercana a los 90 millones de dólares por temporada que sacudió el tablero del mercado deportivo en Colombia. Hasta entonces, Win Sports venía pagando un monto estimado entre 55 y 60 millones de dólares anuales por los derechos del FPC. De acuerdo con lo expuesto por Carlos Antonio Vélez, la cadena televisiva presentó su oferta en solitario —pasadas las 3:30 p. m. de ese viernes— para continuar al frente de la señal oficial. En su versión, el canal cuenta con músculo financiero propio y respaldo de sus socios nacionales e internacionales para afrontar la negociación sin depender de terceros. Según esta versión, la oferta económica de Win Sports iguala y supera ligeramente el umbral de los 90 millones de dólares anuales, cifra que marca un salto drástico frente a los montos que venía pagando el canal en el convenio vigente (ubicados en un rango aproximado de entre 55 y 60 millones de dólares por año). La recta final de las conversaciones estuvo marcada por versiones que aseguraban una supuesta alianza entre Win Sports y Caracol Televisión (incluyendo su plataforma digital Ditu) para sumar músculo financiero y repartirse la operación de las transmisiones. Sin embargo, Caracol Televisión salió al paso y desmintió categóricamente formar parte de cualquier sociedad o alianza con Win Sports o Ditu en esta puja por los derechos del fútbol colombiano. Analistas y comentaristas deportivos también señalaron que Win Sports cuenta con respaldo financiero propio de sus accionistas para asumir el compromiso sin depender de socios externos en esa oferta. Por su parte, el presidente de la Federación Colombiana de Fútbol (FCF), Ramón Jesurún, confirmó que el trámite seguía su curso institucional dentro de los plazos establecidos para que el canal vigente ejerciera su derecho preferencial, dejando la última palabra en manos de la asamblea de la Dimayor. Más allá del monto global del contrato, la votación de los 36 clubes en Bogotá se jugará en varios frentes sensibles que determinarán el impacto real de este acuerdo en el ecosistema del fútbol colombiano: Alcance y cobertura: Definir con precisión qué competiciones quedan incluidas en el paquete y bajo qué condiciones se manejan tanto las transmisiones nacionales como las señales internacionales. Reparto del dinero entre clubes: Persiste el debate interno entre un grupo de clubes tradicionales (los llamados "ocho grandes") que promueve un modelo de distribución más ligado al mérito deportivo y al rating/audiencia, frente a otro bloque de instituciones de primera y segunda división que prefiere conservar esquemas más equitativos. Impacto para el hincha: El aumento sustancial en el costo anual de los derechos abre interrogantes sobre si el nuevo contrato traerá ajustes en las tarifas de suscripción o en los modelos de acceso para los aficionados que siguen los partidos por televisión y plataformas digitales.

articles.title: Bob Chesney reveals message to UCLA after heartbreaking Michigan loss
articles.summary: The UCLA Bruins’ undefeated season is no more after the team suffered an 18-16 overtime loss in Week 12 to the Michigan Wolverines. After the tough loss, hea...
articles.body:
The UCLA Bruins' undefeated season is no more after the team suffered an 18-16 overtime loss in Week 12 to the Michigan Wolverines. After the tough loss, head coach Bob Chesney revealed the message he shared with his team.

The 49-year-old informed Bruins players not to take the loss too harshly . It was a hard-fought battle that didn't end in UCLA's favor, but Chesney wants his players to face reality and put the loss in the rearview mirror.

"The message in the locker room was, nobody hang your head," Chesney said. "You played a really good team, and you battled… When you have your opportunity, you've got to make the most of it against a really good defense like that. And we just didn't do it."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

UCLA's loss throws a wrench in the Big Ten , as a window of opportunity opens for several teams to clinch a spot in the Conference Championship Game with just one week remaining in the regular season. The good news is the Bruins hold their own fate, as a win over the USC Trojans in Week 13 clinches a spot in the Big Ten title game for the program.

Saturday's loss to Michigan marked just the third time this season UCLA failed to score at least 20 points in a game. Although it's been a roller coaster of a campaign for the Wolverines, the team does have one of the best defenses in the nation. That showed against the Bruins, as Chesney's offense struggled to move the ball down the field throughout the contest.

articles.title: Cowboys' botched tackle attempt leads to easy Titans TD
articles.summary: What should have been a routine play for the Cowboys' struggling defense turned to a regrettable miscue as the Titans raced for an easy TD.
articles.body:
Even a change in defensive play-caller can't save the Dallas Cowboys from tackling miscues.

In the third quarter of Sunday's matchup against the Tennessee Titans, Cowboys cornerback Cobie Durant appeared to think he had wide receiver Carnell Tate down by contact after touching his opponent with two hands.

Tate, however, managed to get off the ground just prior to Durant's contact.

With the cornerback letting up, Tate then ran the remaining nearly 50 yards untouched for a 59-yard touchdown.

It marked the first major breakdown for the unit under the leadership of Mike Pettine, who was handed defensive play-calling duties this past week after they were stripped from defensive coordinator Christian Parker.

Tate also ignited another big gain for Tennessee earlier in the third quarter, when he drew a 38-yard pass interference penalty on Cowboys safety Caleb Downs that led to a 1-yard touchdown plunge by Cam Ward.

Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf was ejected in the third quarter of the Steelers' Week 11 contest against the Philadelphia Eagles. It is the third career ejection for Metcalf.

Metcalf could now be facing a suspension by the league for the second straight year. Last season, he was suspended for the final two regular season games after slapping a fan in Detroit. In a similar incident involving players, Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase was suspended for spitting on Jalen Ramsey last season. While his suspension isn't automatic, it's safe to assume the league will review the incident and decide whether or not they will keep him out for at least one game.

articles.title: Will the Browns Make the Playoffs? What Cleveland Needs to Happen During Bye
articles.summary: Where the Browns stand in the AFC and who to root for during their bye week. The post Will the Browns Make the Playoffs? What Cleveland Needs to Happen Durin...
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns needed only 10 games to beat their preseason win projection, and they could climb to the AFC's No. 6 seed Sunday without playing a snap.

At 6-4, Cleveland holds the AFC's final wild-card spot, one game ahead of the New England Patriots. Both teams are on their bye, so the Browns will still be in playoff position when the Las Vegas Raiders come to town next Sunday. Staying there is another matter.

Browns Have Already Beaten the Odds Under Todd Monken

Back in July, Browns owner Jimmy Haslam said he'd take the over on Cleveland's projected 5.5 wins. That took some faith in first-year head coach Todd Monken, who inherited a 5-12 team and put four rookies in the starting lineup on offense.

Rookie pass catchers Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion have been at the top of their class, leading first-year receivers. Boston has 523, followed by KC Concepcion with 458. Two other rookies have been protecting Deshaun Watson, with Spencer Fano at left tackle and Austin Barber at right guard.

Watson has led the winning fourth-quarter drive in each of Cleveland's six victories. The Browns have gone 10 games without scoring on their opening possession , and their most comfortable win came by four points.

Browns Get Three Straight at Home, Starting With Raiders

Cleveland played six of its first nine games on the road. Now the Browns, who are 4-0 at Huntington Bank Field, can go more than a month between road trips. They beat Houston at home before the bye and return Nov. 29 to face the Raiders and No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza. The NFL moved kickoff to 8:20 p.m. ET for NBC's "Sunday Night Football."

The AFC North-leading Cincinnati Bengals (7-2) visit Dec. 6, followed by the Atlanta Falcons on Dec. 13. The first is an important AFC North matchup, with the second coming against the team's former head coach, Kevin Stefanski.

"With that four-game stretch, we can make a move and really build momentum into those other divisional games at the end of the year," Monken said when the schedule came out in May .

Who Should Browns Fans Root for on Sunday?

Philadelphia can do Cleveland the biggest favor against the Steelers. An Eagles win would drop Pittsburgh to 6-4. The Browns and Steelers split their two meetings, so the next tiebreaker is division record. Cleveland's current 2-1 mark beats Pittsburgh's 2-2 and would move the Browns into the sixth seed.

A Carolina win would send Baltimore to 4-7 ahead of its December rematch with Cleveland. The Browns won the first meeting 13-10 and can sweep the season series in Baltimore on Dec. 27. The Ravens are navigating quarterback Lamar Jackson being on IR and potentially out for the year.

The division race carries over to Monday night, when the Bengals visit Washington. A Commanders win would bring Cleveland within one game of Cincinnati, with both head-to-head meetings still to come.

articles.title: Luis Gil leaves Yankees for American League rivals on $2.3 million contract
articles.summary: The 2023 AL Rookie of the Year was non-tendered on Friday.
articles.body:
Two days after the New York Yankees decided not to tender a 2027 contract to pitcher Luis Gil, the 2024 American League Rookie of the Year is on the move.

Gil and the Detroit Tigers are in agreement on a one-year, $2.3 million contract, according to multiple reports.

Gil's deal, pending physical, includes up to $2 million in performance bonuses according to Jeff Passan of ESPN , who was first to report the agreement Sunday, Nov. 22.

Friday marked the deadline for teams to tender 2027 contracts to their arbitration-eligible players. Gil immediately became one of the best available players on the market when the Yankees decided to move on without him. The Boston Red Sox were reportedly interested in Gil as well.

Gil is 21-11 with a 3.61 ERA across five MLB seasons, all with the Yankees. He has made three postseason starts in his career, but did not pitch in the Yankees' American League wild-card series against the Boston Red Sox, or their AL Division Series against the Tampa Bay Rays in October.

A right-handed pitcher, Gil went 1-2 with a 4.61 ERA in nine games (four starts) for New York in 2026. He pitched another three games in the minors but missed most of the season recovering from a shoulder injury.

Gil, 28, was eligible for salary arbitration — and likely a significant raise on his $2.2 million salary — for the second time in his career.

The Tigers will feature a much younger starting rotation in 2027 than in 2026, when they went 76-86 and missed the postseason for the first time since 2023.

Besides Gil, manager A.J. Hinch can turn to right-hander River Ryan, 24-year-old Jackson Jobe, and 26-year-olds Troy Melton and Keider Montero behind 33-year-old Framber Valdez.

Melton and the Tigers reportedly agreed to a six-year, $46.5 million extension on Saturday.

articles.title: Bayern Munich CEO backtracks on statement suggesting a pay cut for Jamal Musiala
articles.summary: The FC Bayern top brass are beginning to realise their blunder
articles.body:
Over the last few days, Bayern Munich's management has engaged in a public discussion about Jamal Musiala's health and whether he will ever return to his previous level. Amid these discussions, CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen suggested that Musiala taking a potential pay cut may be on the cards . Facing quick backlash from fans and others for the comment, Dreesen is now beginning to backtrack.

"Jamal is a player we have particularly high hopes for, and we obviously want him to return to the level he was at when we extended his contract. Perhaps that is also an expression of those expectations. But this has absolutely nothing to do with putting pressure on him. That wouldn't make any sense at all. When a player returns from injury — and here we're talking exclusively about the injury, not the absence seizures — he needs time," said Dreesen (as captured via @iMiaSanMia ).

He continued: "I did not say that we need to revisit his contract; I just explained that Jamal was injured for two months and is now returning. I also already answered your earlier question about whether we or anyone else had any knowledge of this [before the contract extension]. We had no knowledge of it, and I've answered that clearly. So there's no need to discuss contracts. We have a contract in place until 2030. It's absolutely clear, and therefore there is no discussion to be had about that."

This clarification from Dreesen gives the impression that Bayern are now struggling to do damage control after realizing the severity of their blunder by holding these discussions in public. It doesn't help his case, and it looks as though things could play out to be quite messy. What do you think of Dreesen trying to walk back his comments, and how will all of this end? Tell us in the comments below!

Mike Brown made a declaration about Mikal Bridges after the latter made a game-winning shot at the buzzer in the New York Knicks' 97-96 win over the Portland Trail Blazers on Saturday night.

Bridges has been playing in the NBA since 2018, going through his third season with the Knicks. He plays a key role on both sides of the ball on the wing, helping the team reach the mountaintop in 2026.

Bridges is going through a tough start this season, seeing his scoring dive down to single-digits. That didn't stop him from coming through against Portland, seeing Brown talk about his resilience after the game.

"But he's not going to get too high. He's not going to get too low," Brown said. "So for him to have the ball in his hands at that point in the game, there's a lot of confidence not only coming from him but from his teammates and the staff."

articles.title: How Jeff Lebby will decide who is Mississippi State QB in Egg Bowl
articles.summary: Mississippi State coach Jeff Lebby explained how he will decide whether AJ Swann or Billy Puckett start at quarterback in the Egg Bowl vs Ole Miss
articles.body:
STARKVILLE – Mississippi State football is in another week of uncertainty over who will start at quarterback.

This time, it's between injured AJ Swann or Billy Puckett , who got the start in the win against Tennessee Tech.

The decision from coach Jeff Lebby could have big implications as the Bulldogs (5-6, 2-6 SEC) face No. 19 Ole Miss (7-4, 4-4) in the Egg Bowl at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium on Nov. 27 (11 a.m., ABC). A win would clinch bowl eligibility and also give MSU its first win in the rivalry since 2022.

"It will really depend on how AJ is able to practice this week," Lebby said on Nov. 22 "If he's able to really go (Monday) to be able to get to work, then I'll start getting closer to making that decision. But that's really what it's going to be about is if he can go practice. If AJ can't practice at all for us this week, I think it's going to be really hard for him to just go play. So, we'll work through that as we move through the week."

Mississippi State football vs Tennessee Tech, Billy Puckett, Anthony Evans III top photos

The team is holding a walk-through Nov. 22 before practicing Nov. 23. The first SEC availability report for the game will release on Nov. 24.

Swann and Puckett have started multiple games because of star Kamario Taylor's season-ending injury. Neither have been perfect solutions for the offense though as MSU carried a six-game losing streak until beating Tennessee Tech, 34-16.

Swann, the Appalachian State transfer, started three straight games against Texas, Vanderbilt and Auburn but got injured in the first half vs Auburn. He had a boot on his left foot while standing on the sideline against Tennessee Tech.

Puckett, who walked on to the team last year, had his best game of the season against Tennessee Tech with 232 yards passing, two touchdowns, an interception and 25 rushing yards.

Ole Miss ' defense ranks 10th in the SEC in scoring with 25.0 points per game and 14th in yardage at 368.9 per game. The Rebels have 26 sacks, tied for 10th in the SEC, and have the conference's worst run defense with 152.2 yards allowed per game.

"We've got to do a great job taking care of the football," Lebby said. "That's where it's going to start, and that starts again up front. They don't touch the ball, but we've got to do everything we can to keep the quarterback upright and clean from a pass protection standpoint. That will be a great challenge.

"I don't think there's any doubt the front for Ole Miss is the best part of their defense. And so, for us, we're going to have to play really well up front and going to have to be better than we've been fundamentally and protect the QB in a great way."

articles.body:
Atlético-MG will cover the cost of returning to Brazil for a group of fans who traveled in a VW Kombi van to the Copa Sudamericana final, in which the team lost to Boca Juniors.

The story of Igor Batista, Daniel Marques and Emerson Coelho attracted attention after they took 17 days to reach Barranquilla, Colombia, where the match was held.

The club contacted them to say it would pay for flights for all three and arrange to transport the vehicle back to Brazil.

According to ge, Igor revealed on social media that Atlético's communications director, Domênico Bhering, was the one who called to tell them the club would cover their transportation costs.

The group of fans was already preparing to hit the road and begin the journey back to Brazil when they received the call.

Igor, Daniel and Emerson traveled more than 7,000 kilometers to watch the Copa Sudamericana final, passing through three countries on a route that included three days of ferry travel.

Upon arriving in Barranquilla, they were honored by the club and took part in an event with players from Atlético's squad.

articles.title: Steelers' DK Metcalf ejected for controversial altercation with Eagles' Cooper DeJean
articles.summary: DK Metcalf was just ejected from the Pittsburgh Steelers' Week 11 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles.
articles.body:
Yikes! Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf was just disqualified from the Week 11 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles — here's what fans should know.

With less than five minutes remaining in the third quarter, Metcalf was involved in a heated altercation with Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean, where it appeared Metcalf was jamming his fingers into the face of DeJean, prompting the officials to flag him for unsportsmanlike conduct. Metcalf was ultimately ejected from the game, leaving the Steelers down to Germie Bernard and Roman Wilson as their top wide receiving threats.

Earlier in the game, Metcalf and DeJean got into a heated altercation that ultimately resulted in DK receiving an unnecessary roughness penalty.

Metcalf, who was traded from the Seahawks to the Steelers in March 2025, has failed to live up to his $132 million extension, in large part due to his inconsistent play and immature antics on the field.

From dropped balls to costly penalties, Metcalf's actions have to be heavily wearing out the Steelers' patience, so much so that it begs the question: How much longer will Pittsburgh put up with paying him top wide receiver money without the production?

articles.title: Everything Luke Fickell said after Badgers win over Purdue
articles.summary: Wisconsin’s head coach broke down the win after the game.
articles.body:
The Wisconsin Badgers blew out the Purdue Boilermakers 42-10 on Saturday, improving to 7-4 as they bounced back from their loss to the Maryland Terrapins.

Wisconsin dominated every part of the game. They gained over 500 yards on offense, including 381 yards and five touchdowns on the ground, while the defense didn't even allow 200 yards.

After the game, head coach Luke Fickell spoke to reporters, breaking down what he saw from his team.

Earlier in the week, I reminded our team that this is a really good football team, and our job is to act like it, attack like it, and play like it. That's what we did today.

I'm proud of everybody, but especially the offensive line and the offense. They've heard questions all year about injuries, lineup changes, and consistency, and they took that personally. They played with a chip on their shoulder, and that mentality started with the quarterback and spread throughout the offense.

That was the type of complementary football we're capable of playing. We just need to do it more consistently. I believe we have the leadership and the pieces necessary to keep building. You also saw some young players today, particularly on the offensive line and in the secondary, who represent the future of this program.

What really stood out was how the players handled this past week. I said before the game that we had a good week of preparation, and our guys showed tremendous attitude and resilience. They kept working, kept battling, and kept each other up.

Now we have to continue to build from this. If you can go on the road, establish the run, create momentum up front, and generate energy early, it opens up a lot of things offensively. That's exactly what happened today.

On how Colton Joseph handled everything throughout the week…

Colte=on isn't somebody who wears his emotions on his sleeve. He internalizes a lot of things, so sometimes it's difficult to know exactly what he's feeling.

What I can say is that he continued to work, continued to respond to challenges, and answered the bell every step of the way. I challenged him in a lot of different areas, and he never backed down.

I can't say enough about how appreciative I am of him or how proud I am of the way he's handled everything. His teammates recognize that too.

On the significance of earning a road win and building confidence…

You have to feel good about it because this league is a battle every single week. We knew going in that we were facing a good offense and that the game would be a fight. We were able to turn it into something a little different as the game went on, but there was never any misconception about the challenge.

You can tell players they're a good football team as much as you want, but at some point they need to see it for themselves. Seeing is believing.

I'm happy for our guys because now they can feel what that success looks like. The challenge becomes building on it because every week in this league is going to require the ability to handle adversity and respond to difficult situations.

On Blake Cherry and the offensive line's performance…

Blake Cherry earned that opportunity and stepped up. He started the season at right guard against Notre Dame but suffered a high ankle sprain that really limited him and prevented him from getting consistent opportunities afterward.

We had originally discussed rotating more players, but before the game I told Coach Mateos I didn't want to see much rotation. I wanted to let that group settle in, get rolling, and establish a rhythm.

From the opening drive, they set a tone. They played aggressively, attacked the line of scrimmage, and it was noticeable from the start.

On Darrion Dupree's performance and becoming the featured back…

I'm incredibly proud of Darrion. At some point, you have to stop worrying about labels and simply decide who you're going to ride with. We know what we're going to get from Darrion. It's going to be physical, downhill football, and smart decision-making.

He's an all-around complete back because he can run the ball, protect on third downs, and contribute in a variety of situations.

We still need to be smart about using other backs and preserving his workload, but he's our guy. I've seen what he can do for a long time. Maybe he hasn't always had enough opportunities to show everybody else, but he's shown us consistently.

On improved third-down success and Colten Joseph's aggressiveness…

A lot of it starts with staying out of third-and-long situations.

When you're facing third-and-four, third-and-five, third-and-six, or even third-and-seven, the offense has a lot more options than it does in third-and-12 or third-and-nine.

The protection was also significantly better, and the offensive line deserves credit for that. I thought Colton played aggressively as well. He wasn't simply looking to throw the football. When lanes opened up, he was willing to run. He also did a good job of extending plays, creating opportunities, and keeping his eyes downfield.

That combination gives us many more options offensively and makes us harder to defend.

On Ryan Hopkins 's status and why he did not play more…

Ryan didn't fully clear protocol until later in the week.

We generally knew what our plan would be, but we also wanted to keep some things close to the vest and see exactly where Ryan was physically before making any final decisions. Beyond the protocol situation, he was also still dealing with soreness on his non-throwing side from the hit he took previously.

He didn't receive many practice reps this week because of those circumstances. The expectation is that moving forward he'll be back in the mix and available again next week.

On the performance of the injury-depleted secondary…

A lot of credit goes to Coach Steeples, Coach Haynes, Coach Cooper, and [Coach Tressel] for the work they did preparing and mixing those players into different roles throughout the week.

Donovan Dunnmore stepped up, and in a lot of ways, you're starting to see what the future of that secondary looks like. We certainly miss some of the veterans who are unavailable, but these young players are gaining valuable experience.

I'm especially proud of Jai'mier. He didn't play the previous week, was still dealing with injuries throughout the week, and there were legitimate questions about whether he would be able to go.

All he did was prepare, get his mind right, and put himself in a position to contribute. There's a lot of youth in that back end, but there's also a lot to be excited about for the future.

On the message to the team with Minnesota and rivalry week ahead…

I really didn't need to say much because the players handled it themselves in the locker room.

A lot of the leaders talked before the season about their goals for this program, and it was never solely about records, standings, or playoff scenarios. Rivalry games have always been a major part of what this group wanted to accomplish.

The leadership in that locker room is continuing to reveal itself, and that's been one of the most encouraging parts of this season. It's going to be a short week, but it's going to be a great week.

On adjusting the schedule for a short week…

We'll definitely have to make some adjustments.

The quick turnaround changes things, particularly because of when we practice and how the week is structured. We'll enjoy this win, but we also understand it's time to move on quickly and get ready for the next challenge.

On Eugene Hilton's growing role in the offense…

Eugene is a player, and we need to continue finding ways to get the ball in his hands.

He's extremely versatile and has the ability to impact the game in multiple ways. When you talk about the future of this team and where the program is headed, Eugene is one of the young players who represents that future.

The talent is obvious, and we have to continue creating opportunities for him because he can change games.

On Marvin Burks's expanded role in the secondary…

Marv had to take on significantly more responsibility with Matt Jung unavailable.

That required him to move around, play multiple positions, and handle duties that we may not have envisioned for him earlier in the season.

He embraced all of it and stepped up when the team needed him most. The flexibility he's shown and the way he's handled those challenges have been invaluable for us.

articles.title: Boston Celtics at Golden State Warriors: Stream, lineups, injury reports, broadcast (11/22)
articles.summary: The Boston Celtics will look to avoid their fourth straight loss when they face the Golden State Warriors on Sunday night.
articles.body:
In past regular seasons, the Boston Celtics have generally churned out win after win, especially under head coach Joe Mazzulla. However, after resting multiple key players against the struggling Sacramento Kings on Saturday night and falling to them, 97-96, the C's are at risk of losing four games in a row. That'd be enough for Boston's longest losing streak since the 2020-21 season, which was back when de facto Celtics general manager Brad Stevens was still the head coach of the Green Team.

Such a skid can be avoided if the 11-5 Celtics are able to topple the 8-8 Golden State Warriors on Sunday evening in San Francisco. The C's may be tired because they're playing on the second night of a back-to-back — their fourth time doing so this November — but attempting to bounce back from arguably their worst defeat of the season could serve as motivation. Although, one could say the same about the Warriors, who are currently on a five-game losing streak (the longest active slide in the Western Conference) that's coincided with the injury absence of star point guard Stephen Curry. The future Hall of Famer won't return versus the Celtics, but star forward Jayson Tatum could take the floor again for Boston after resting on Saturday. No matter who plays, the C's should expect a tough battle from a rested Warriors squad in one of the loudest arenas in the NBA.

The Celtics have dropped three consecutive contests and are 11-5 overall. Despite this lull, they remain in second place in the Eastern Conference.

The Dubs have lost five straight games and hold a .500 record (8-8). For the moment, they sit just outside of Play-In territory with the eleventh seed in the West.

The Celtics have yet to submit an injury report for Saturday's outing in San Fran.

Meanwhile, the Warriors reported several significant injuries, as Curry (right oblique tear), Kristaps Porzingis (illness and not with the team), Jimmy Butler (right ACL repair), Moses Moody (left patellar tendon repair), and Brandon Williams (left hamstring strain) are all listed as out.

articles.title: Four Prime Candidates Likely To Replace Luis Castillo and Davis Martin
articles.summary: The Chicago White Sox shipped veteran right-handers Luis Castillo and Davis Martin to the Colorado Rockies in a four-player swap on Thursday. The trade means...
articles.body:
The Chicago White Sox shipped veteran right-handers Luis Castillo and Davis Martin to the Colorado Rockies in a four-player swap on Thursday. The trade means the entirety of Castillo's remaining $22.75 million guarantee for 2027, after posting an 8.42 ERA down the stretch for Chicago, will now be paid by the Rockies. GM Chris Getz parting with Martin, the longest-tenured player who posted a 3.95 ERA over 146 innings, was seen as a ruthless move, but the Rockies weren't willing to take Castillo without Martin. That is the price of doing business in the modern baseball market.

‎However, Martin's lingering right calf issue may be one reason Getz agreed to trade him. It is hard to predict whether the 29-year-old will deliver 2026-level production next year, given that injuries have been his biggest letdown over the past three years. Now, with roughly $25 million off the White Sox payroll, two sudden openings in Will Venable's starting rotation need to be filled.

This is when the real work begins because replacing Castillo and Martin isn't a simple one-for-one swap. It requires balancing immediate playoff-caliber innings with extensive experience in commanding the zone, and already-made pitchers with an illustrious career record.

Getz's maneuvering of Luis Castillo's contract to save $25 million is one of the most genius moves this offseason. But it will become a masterstroke should he use the cash to acquire a top-of-the-rotation ace. Tarik Skubal is poised to command a record-shattering $350 million-plus mega-deal, which the White Sox cannot meet. But Chicago's financial window can easily take in right-handers Freddy Peralta or Michael King . Both players are projected around a $24 million to $30 million a year deal, nearly as identical to what they could have paid Castillo.

So, the big question is between Peralta and King: who will be the ideal signing for the White Sox? ‎Several factors point towards Peralta as the ideal stylistic replacement for Castillo. The 30-year-old shook off a sluggish first-half 2026 start with the Tampa Bay Rays following a trade deadline move from the New York Mets. Peralta offers the Sox a six-year track record of sub-4.00 ERAs and elite whiff rates without costing the franchise a draft pick.

Though King brings a fresher arm with experience, Peralta looks like the best choice. In fact, King wouldn't be a bad choice at all should the White Sox sign him. Since transitioning from the New York Yankees bullpen to a starter, his advanced metrics have been on the rise. But he might be a riskier signing than Peralta outside of San Diego's strongly built pitching system.

The White Sox have been heavily linked to two fascinating Japanese right-handers: Kaima Taira and Hiromi Itoh . Both pitchers have a strong track record as top-tier starters in Japan. Itoh has pitched in at least 140 innings in each of his six seasons with the Hokkaido Nippon-Ham Fighters. He's listed at 5-foot-9 and 180 pounds, which sets him up for an impeccable command of the zone. From 2021 to 2026, he posted a 2.92 ERA over 1,000 innings pitched, with 902 strikeouts and a 1.169 WHIP. However, in 2026, his performance took a step backward as he posted a 3.18 ERA and a 1.263 WHIP over his 172 2/3 innings, striking out 159 batters with 34 walks.

‎Taira, on the other hand, is 27, which means he's at his peak physical condition. Across eight seasons in the NPB, he posted 9.4 strikeouts per nine innings. Besides that, in 2026, with the Saitama Seibu Lions, he went 12-5 with the Japanese league's best record (1.36 ERA) and 141 strikeouts across 146 innings.

Both players are valued between $10 million and $20 million in the market, which is not too much for the White Sox to spend. The only issue with acquiring either Taira or Itoh is that they cannot become instant starters. They will need a few months to adjust to the major league pitching standard and find their durability on the mound before becoming starters.

Trading away a clubhouse pillar like Martin is a big pain for the White Sox, particularly when you look at how much he went through from April to May, pitching through an injury to keep the rotation afloat. But sentiments don't win baseball matches, especially in October. And the Castillo trade was the best choice for the White Sox. So, Getz has to look at what's squarely in front of him and what he has to do to give the rotation the depth it needs.

‎Also, Grant Taylor has to be handed a fifth starter job for protection, whilst acquiring top-tier pitchers that slot alongside Dustin May and Sean Burke . The White Sox can become a powerhouse in the American League if the right players are signed and solid competition is engineered in the clubhouse.

articles.title: Bussi makes 25 saves and Hurricanes down Rangers 5-2
articles.summary: NEW YORK (AP) — Jackson Blake put Carolina ahead to stay midway through the second period and Brandon Bussi made 25 saves and the Carolina Hurricanes defeate...
articles.body:
NEW YORK (AP) — Jackson Blake put Carolina ahead to stay midway through the second period and Brandon Bussi made 25 saves and the Carolina Hurricanes defeated the New York Rangers 5-2 on Sunday.

Blake snapped a 1-1 tie on the backhand at 13:13, followed in quick succession by goals from defensemen Alexander Nikishin and Sean Walker as the first-place Hurricanes won for the sixth time in seven games.

Mika Zibanejad and J.T. Miller scored for the Rangers, who had their three-game winning streak snapped.

Eric Robinson also scored for the defending champion Hurricanes, who are an Eastern Conference-best 18-3-3.

Robinson opened the scoring with a short-handed goal at the 13-minute mark of the first, beating Rangers netminder Dylan Garand for his third goal.

Zibanejad tied it on the power play at 14:12 of the opening period with his sixth goal. The 33-year-old Zibanejad is sixth in Rangers history with 687 points, four points behind Mark Messier for fifth place.

Blake put the visitors ahead finishing off a passing play with linemates Taylor Hall and Logan Stankoven for his seventh goal.

Nikishin made it 3-1 at 17:46. Walker, playing his 500th game, extended the lead to 4-1 at 18:27.

Miller made it 4-2 on the power play at 15:13 of the third before Jordan Martinook scored into an empty net.

The Rangers hadn't played since Monday's 3-1 home win over Montreal. New York lost for only the third time in 12 games at Madison Square Garden.

Bussi, who won 31 games last season and three in the Cup Final after he was claimed off waivers, improved to 5-2-2.

Rangers newcomer Max Sasson — acquired Friday from Vancouver — skated on a line with Glenn Gawdin and Matt Rempe.

Rangers forward Pavel Dorofeyev missed his second straight game with a lower-body injury.

articles.title: Steelers’ DK Metcalf ejected vs Eagles after epic meltdown

Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf has had a terrible, horrible, no good, very bad season so far. This continued against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 11. The former Seattle Seahawk hasn't built chemistry with Aaron Rodgers and has caught only two touchdown passes this season.

Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf was ejected in the second half against the Philadelphia Eagles after receiving his second personal foul.

Metcalf was anything but productive in this Week 11 matchup. He caught only one pass for two yards and didn't seem focused on playing football this week.

Steelers fans and Metcalf's fantasy football managers have to be asking what is going on with the Pittsburgh wideout. Rodgers and the rest of the offense need him out there because he can truly be a game changer. He won't be able to do that this time, since he'll be watching from the locker room.
