articles.body:
The Detroit Tigers ' rotation continues to take shape, as the team reportedly signed right-hander Luis Gil to a one-year deal on Sunday, Nov. 22.

The deal is reportedly worth $2.3 million for the 2027 season and also includes performances bonuses that could be worth up to $2 million.

Gil was non-tendered by the New York Yankees on Friday, just about two years after being named the 2024 American Rookie of the Year. That season, he posted a 3.50 ERA while striking out 171 and walking an MLB-worst 77 batters in 151⅔ innings over 29 starts.

But the 28-year-old has dealt with numerous injuries in the two seasons since, limiting him to just 84⅓ innings in 2025 and 2026. That included 27⅓ innings last season, when he had a 4.61 ERA with more walks (18) than strikeouts (17).

Gil missed the first four months of the 2025 season with a serious lat strain. He started 2026 healthy, but landed back on the injured list in April with a right shoulder inflammation, returning to the Yankees in late August.

He moved to the bullpen while rehabbing in Triple-A and recorded a 3.00 ERA with 12 strikeouts and seven walks in five appearances. Upon his return to the majors, he was marginally more effective, with his 1.13 ERA and eight strikeouts in eight innings over five relief appearances belied by seven walks and a hit-by-pitch.

The deal comes two days after the Tigers locked in the apparent top of their rotation by giving 25-year-old right-hander Troy Melton a six-year extension worth $46.5 million.

Melton and left-hander Framber Valdez should headline the Tigers staff, followed by right-hander Jackson Jobe and right-hander Keider Montero. Right-handed swingman Drew Anderson, who posted a 2.61 ERA in 11 starts, with nine coming after the All-Star break, is expected to fight for a starting role, and righty River Ryan, who joined the organization in the trade that sent lefty Tarik Skubal to the Los Angeles Dodgers, should also be a rotation contender.

This is a breaking news story and will be updated.

articles.title: Ravens’ Lamar Jackson is fired up over Devontez Walker’s kick return TD vs. Panthers
articles.summary: On Sunday afternoon, the Baltimore Ravens hit the field on the road vs the Carolina Panthers, looking to pick up their first win in several weeks. Lamar Jac...
articles.body:
On Sunday afternoon, the Baltimore Ravens hit the field on the road vs the Carolina Panthers , looking to pick up their first win in several weeks. Lamar Jackson was once again sidelined in this one with a thumb injury, opening the door for Jacoby Brissett to get another start.

At one point in the first half, Ravens kick returner Devontez Walker returned a kickoff all the way to the house to put the Ravens up 19-14 on the road.

Jackson, who was watching the game from home, took to X, formerly Twitter, to show love for the big play.

"Tezzzzzz walk em no walker!!!!!" he wrote on the social media platform.

The epic play left the fans in attendance in Charlotte stunned, as the two teams continued to trade punches throughout the rest of the first half.

The Ravens entered this game with a record of 4-6 on the season, having lost four games in a row amid Jackson's injury struggles, which began with an ankle issue suffered vs the Tennessee Titans and then continued in his first game back when he suffered a thumb injury.

The Ravens recently traded for Brissett in an attempt to give themselves some semblance of solid QB play, but that wasn't enough to stop the Los Angeles Chargers from picking up their first win of the season vs Baltimore last week.

However, if Walker and some other unsung heroes continue to make explosive plays like this, the Ravens could end up getting themselves back into the mix while Jackson remains sidelined.

articles.title: Jameson Williams raises eyebrows by front-flipping into end zone week after Aidan Hutchinson's injury
articles.summary: If the Lions told their players to tone down the celebrations after Aidan Hutchinson's ill-fated moment, the message didn't get through to Jameson Williams.
articles.body:
Aidan Hutchinson's season-ending ACL tear suffered while celebrating a sack changed the way some players approach celebrations, with Giants RB Cam Skattebo already saying he won't backflip into the end zone anymore.

Hutchinson's teammate, Lions WR Jameson Williams, did not get that message.

Williams raised some eyebrows by front-flipping into the end zone a week after Hutchinson went down, and his awkward landing had to give coach Dan Campbell a headache.

Here's a look at the ill-timed celebration.

Jameson Williams front-flips into end zone

A big-play touchdown is worthy of celebration, but Williams gave Lions fans a scare with his front-flip into the end zone against the Buccaneers on Sunday:

To make matters worse, Williams didn't cleanly land the flip, awkwardly slipping to the turf in a moment that couldn't have been fun to watch for any Lions coach.

The celebration came a week after Hutchinson saw his season end after sacking Drake Maye in Munich — not from the sack itself, but from an awkward landing after leaping into the air in celebration.

The moment was a reminder that going airborne to celebrate a play might not be worthwhile, but Williams clearly has no problem sticking with his approach.

articles.title: Well, That’s Better: Marquette 106, Chicago State 62
articles.summary: The hot shooting Golden Eagles set a new record for three-pointers in a game and never trailed after a 10-0 start.
articles.body:
When Colin Porter missed a three-pointer with 14:10 left to go in the first half, that went into the scorebooks as Marquette's first missed field goal of the game. Yes, nearly six straight minutes without missing a shot. Your score at the time: Marquette 22, Chicago State 10. The Golden Eagles had just answered a 5-0 CSU burst with nine straight before the Cougars cashed in a three-pointer to break up that run.

For the next few minutes, it was actually a back and forth basketball game. From the 12 minute mark of the first half until there was under eight minutes left, neither team scored two buckets in a row. That left Marquette up just 12 points even though they had led by as many as 17 at one point.

And then Marquette discovered the EVAPORATE button.

10 straight for the Golden Eagles, with Royce Parham hitting two three-pointers along the way. Then a free throw from CSU's Mike Price, then a three from Michael Phillips, then a layup from CSU's Foday Sheriff, then another 10 straight points from Marquette to end the half.

10-0 run to end the half, or 13-2 if you prefer, or 23-3 if you prefer. Marquette by 32, 57-25, at intermission.

The lead hit 40 for the first time on a triple from Phillips as part of a 9-0 run in the second half as MU blew the margin out to 75-31 with 15:03 to play. That 44 point gap would be the largest lead of the game for Marquette as Chicago State did managed to shave some space off of that, first with an immediate 8-0 run, and back-to-back three-pointers from Davius Loury got the Cougars as close as 34. That's the most that Marquette allowed, and then they closed the game on an 18-8 run. Never more than five at a time, but that's how they ended up back at 44 to end it.

For historic purposes: Ian Miletic got Marquette over the century mark with a three-pointer with 1:38 to go, and that shot tied the program record for threes by a team in a game. Miletic then broke that record with Marquette's 19th three-pointer of the game with 54 seconds left.

Your leading scorer here was Adrien Stevens, who put up 18 points on 6-for-11 shooting, with four of his five misses coming as part of his 5-for-9 three-point shooting on the day. Royce Parham had 16, Sananda Fru and Michael Phillips both had 13, and Nigel James added 11. Nolan Minessale's five rebounds led the Golden Eagles in that column, and James had seven assists in 20 foul-and-margin shortened minutes.

In case you were wondering: Marquette shot 75% on two-pointers here, which is a marked improvement on what they've looked like in general this season. They also grabbed 67% of their rare misses and limited Chicago State to just 39% of their misses, and seeing as offensive rebounding was a CSU strength coming in, that's not too bad.

No matter what, this was definitely better than the performance turned in against Northern Illinois earlier in the week. That was lackluster and missing an edge. We can haggle about degree of opposition, but Marquette didn't let Chicago State off the mat in any fashion after a hot start.

Up Next: We're going to ramp up the difficulty a little bit. On Wednesday morning — yes, morning, except on the East coast — Marquette tips off with Virginia in the first of their two games in the Battle 4 Atlantis. Tipoff is set for 11am Central time, and ESPN will have the broadcast. The Cavaliers are currently ranked #4 in the country and are a perfect 7-0 after beating Loyola Maryland on Friday, 103-61. Given what Houston did in the Players Era event, I think they're going to be #1 on Monday, but Virginia could easily be #2 since Florida, Michigan State, and UConn all lost this week.

articles.title: Gerwyn Price roars to Grand Slam of Darts title with victory over Gian van Veen to end four-year major drought
articles.summary: Gerwyn Price defeated Gian van Veen to win Grand Slam of Darts for fourth time; it is Price's first major title in four years; it moves him up to world No 3 above Luke Humphries
articles.body:
The win continues what has been a brilliant 2026 for Price. The Grand Slam marked his fourth major final of the year after making it to the World Grand Prix, World Matchplay and World Series Finals deciders, but this was his first success.

Price also maintained his perfect record in finals at this tournament, adding to his 2018, 2019 and 2021 triumphs.

It is Price's first major victory since 2022. The win also moves him up to world No 3, overtaking Luke Humphries, with Van Veen world No 2.

With his eighth major win, Price also moves alongside Gary Anderson and Peter Wright in terms of majors won.

Price will now be hoping to continue a four-year-long trend where the winner of the Grand Slam goes on to win the World Darts Championship.

"It's amazing. I've had some close calls this year where I probably should have won games and tournaments, but when it comes along, it's nice," Price told Sky Sports .

"I was probably more nervous in this game than ever. I've lost so many finals and just to keep the media off my back. Now they can stop talking about it and I can go to Minehead next week with a major, so they can leave me alone.

"The sweet thing about this is the last couple of years, whoever won has gone on to win the World [Championship], so...

"If that happens, then I'll take six months out!"

Price scores big for eighth major victory

With the Wolverhampton crowd at fever pitch, they were treated to a to-and-fro opening session. It looked like it was all going to go the way of Price when he powered in a sensational 150 checkout for a second break of throw, but Van Veen held his nerve and broke straight back to go into the first break just 3-2 behind.

Van Veen thought he was on for a two-leg cushion in the second session after breaking Price's throw in the ninth leg but, in typical 'Iceman' fashion, Price fired straight back with a 145 checkout on tops to level things at 5-5.

The standard was high and there was nothing separating them.

While both players were finding some clutch doubling, neither could initially find a strong spell to run away. Van Veen had the first real opportunity to break the throw in the 15th leg but, with both finding trouble down on D2, Price eventually took it to hold and lead 8-7.

Rattling off the next five legs, Price found three breaks of throw and a clutch tops-tops checkout for 100 that left Van Veen without any answers.

In no time, he was three legs away from glory and six legs ahead of Van Veen, his 102.95 average compared to Van Veen's 83.71 for the third session the key statistic.

Van Veen managed to stop the rot with a break of throw but just as he thought he would be able to make it back-to-back breaks, Price took out a clutch 132 checkout on the bull to move 14-9 ahead.

Although Van Veen continued to hold his throw, that was not going to be enough.

The moment arrived at 15-11 and Price decided to win the Grand Slam in some style. With a 118 checkout on tops, his fifth ton-plus finish of the match, Price's crowning moment arrived.

Van Veen: Price puts everyone under pressure

Runner-up Gian van Veen speaking to Sky Sports:

"It has been a very positive week but I am very disappointed. It was a close game and he took out a lot of good finishes. I missed chances.

"I think 16-11 is a flattering scoreline but that's what Gezzy does. He always puts everyone under pressure. He deserved to win."

Becoming world No 3 has done Price a 'favour'

Sky Sports' Dan Dawson on Price's Grand Slam win:

"Price has had to battle to this title and I think he's had to battle to win this Grand Slam more than he has in any other since his first, because we've seen him play unbelievable stuff to win Grand Slam titles.

"But I think that's what he's had to do to become a winner again, and seeing him smile and seeing that pressure lift, just hearing him talk, I think that is an enormous sign because he's already looking ahead. What can I win next?

"We know that at Ally Pally he is up into No 3 in the world, with Luke Humphries and Luke Littler on the same side of the draw provisionally.

"That game there between Gian and Gerwyn Price, that would provisionally be the semi-final in the other half of the draw.

"So that has done him a favour if he is looking to become a world champion again."

articles.title: Grand Slam of Darts 2026 results: Gerwyn Price beats Gian van Veen to end major PDC title wait
articles.summary: Gerwyn Price ends his four-year wait for a major PDC title as he powers to a brilliant 16-11 victory over Gian van Veen in the Grand Slam of Darts final.
articles.body:
Gerwyn Price ended his four-year wait for a major PDC title as he powered to a brilliant 16-11 victory over Gian van Veen in the Grand Slam of Darts final.

The Welshman last won a major title when he claimed the World Series in 2022, but finally got over the line after defeats in three finals in 2026.

The 41-year-old was the runner-up at the World Matchplay, World Grand Prix and World Series, as well as suffering semi-final exits in the Premier League, World Masters, UK Open and European Championships.

This title has been long overdue and Price won it in spectacular fashion with a mid-match burst.

Despite six breaks of throw in the opening 14 legs - including brilliant 150 and 145 checkouts from Price - the game was level at 7-7.

But Price claimed a crucial lead in a scrappy 15th leg when he finally took out double two at the sixth attempt.

That flicked a switch after a mini-interval and Price won the next five legs to open up a six-leg advantage.

Van Veen broke back after another interval, but Price was able to hold off any hopes of a comeback from the Dutchman and seal his fourth Grand Slam title.

"It's amazing - I've had some close calls this year when I probably should have won games and tournaments, but when it finally comes around it's nice," Price, who moves to world number three, told Sky Sports.

"I was probably more nervous in this game than ever. Just to keep the media off my back, I mean I do mind and I don't mind, but just to keep them off my back.

The triumph, which sees Price earn £200,000 and the Eric Bristow Trophy, is his first in a PDC ranking and TV major since he won this event in 2021.

The pair will now switch their focus to the Players Championship Finals from Friday, where they could meet in the second round.

That event will determine Price's place in the PDC order of merit and his seeding for the World Championships which begin on 11 December. The draw takes place on 30 November.

Reaction and analysis as Price wins Grand Slam title

Grand Slam of Darts results & prize money

What does this mean for the World Championship?

Across the 19 editions of the Grand Slam, seven of the winners have gone on to triumph at the World Championship in the weeks that follow.

It has happened in each of the past four years, with Luke Littler (twice), Luke Humphries and Michael Smith doubling up.

The past 10 years have delivered five winners of both in the same season, while another two Grand Slam winners have reached the Worlds semi-finals and one the quarter-finals.

Therefore a Grand Slam winner usually has a pretty decent run at the Worlds, although with Van Veen as second seed and Price either third or fourth, that would hardly be a huge surprise.

Of the 19 World Championship winners since the Grand Slam's inception, 11 have reached at least the semi-finals in Wolverhampton - or Coventry, which staged the 2020 event (seven winners, two runners-ups and two semi-finalists).

The good news for Littler and Humphries, who were both beaten in the last 16 this week, is that five winners of the Worlds have also been knocked out at the same stage of the Slam.

articles.title: England 40-55 Jamaica: Vitality Roses beaten in London as Sunshine Girls impress and level four-Test Horizon Series
articles.summary: Jamaica bounced back from losing their opening match to level the four-Test series against the Vitality Roses; England will travel to Jamaica to play further matches on December 5 and 6, as preparation continues for next year's Netball World Cup
articles.body:
A day on from a dramatic 47-46 victory in the series opener at the same London venue, England were second-best as the Sunshine Girls claimed a comfortable victory and levelled the four-Test series.

The visitors scored six consecutive points on their way to opening a 15-7 advantage after the first quarter, then the Commonwealth Games silver medallists extended their lead to 11 points by half-time.

A tight third quarter saw Jamaica edge further ahead, with the Sunshine Girls never relinquishing their advantage as they closed out a convincing win on away soil.

"We expected Jamaica to come out hard and they certainly did deliver on that," England coach Anna Stembridge admitted.

"We didn't set the tone, we were wasteful at times. We worked through it, but they left us wanting after the first quarter."

England were again without key players Liv Tchine, Alicia Scholes and Sasha Glasgow due to injury, as they had been the previous day, while Jamaica's Latanya Wilson was named player of the match.

Jamaica made 17 gains to England's 11 and had a better shooting percentage than the hosts, who went with the same starting seven as Saturday's victory.

"We started sharper, created more options, we were more aggressive and played to our strengths," Jamaica coach Sasher Gaye Henry-Wright said.

"We didn't stick to our game plan yesterday and today we were more disciplined."

England will now travel to Jamaica for the final two matches of the series, held at the National Indoor Sports Centre in Kingston on December 5 and 6.

articles.title: Gerwyn Price looking to continue trend of Grand Slam victors tasting World Darts Championship glory
articles.summary: Gerwyn Price won the Grand Slam of Darts with a 16-11 victory over Gian van Veen; the last four winners of the Grand Slam have gone on to win the World Darts Championship at Alexandra Palace; Price is hoping to continue the trend
articles.body:
It started with Michael Smith back in 2022, with Luke Humphries continuing it in 2023.

Of course, Luke Littler's back-to-back triumphs in Wolverhampton in 2024 and 2025 were then followed by him lifting the Sid Waddell Trophy.

Gerwyn Price wants to continue that in 2026.

Price roared to a 16-11 victory over Gian van Veen in the final of the Grand Slam, hitting five massive ton-plus checkouts in a confident display.

The win moves Price up to world No 3 ahead of Humphries and marks his first major title in four years.

Alexandra Palace was immediately on Price's mind following his victory and he hopes to extend the trend into a fifth year and become a two-time world champion.

"The sweet thing about this is the last couple of years, whoever won has gone on to win the World [Championship], so....," Price said after beating Van Veen.

"If that happens, then I'll take six months out!"

"I am superstitious and I believe in stuff like that," he later added.

"I hope I am not the one to break the trend."

Price has been in some form in 2026, the Grand Slam marking his fourth major final of the year but his first victory.

The Welshman has maintained he is the most consistent player across 2026 and puts part of that down to the love he now gets from the crowd.

It is a very different story from when he last won a Grand Slam title five years ago.

"How different it is, the crowd right behind me and cheering me all the way. How things can change." Price added.

"I thought these days would happen, I just didn't know when. I am glad it happened sooner rather than later.

"It definitely helps and spurs you on to come out to a crowd who is right behind you rather than against you.

"I have had that for the last two-and-a-half years and hopefully it continues.

"People have just realised I am who I am, I wear my heart on my sleeve, and I don't do things to put people off which people think I did.

"I am the most consistent. I am not saying I am the best player.

"I am full of confidence, I am in some great form. I am the most consistent across this season."

'I have now got the media off my back, not the monkey'

With the form 'The Iceman' has been in, it is remarkable it had been so long since Price had last tasted major glory back in 2022.

While he says it did not bother him, being reminded by the "media" spurred him on.

"You guys [the media] were putting pressure on me and reminding me I hadn't won a tournament in a long time," Price said.

"You probably spurred me on as well so thanks.

"I keep saying I am not bothered when I lose and I stand by that.

"Obviously it hurts to lose. I have now got you off my back, not the monkey."

articles.title: Tarik Skubal agrees to record $450 million contract with New York Mets
articles.summary: Tarik Skubal, the top free agent on the MLB market, has a agreed to record $450 million, nine-year contract with the New York Mets, a source told The Associated Press.
articles.body: Tarik Skubal, the two-time Cy Young Award winner who was the top free agent on this offseason’s market, has a agreed to record $450 million, nine-year contract with the New York Mets, a person familiar the negotiations told The Associated Press on Sunday. The person spoke on condition of anonymity because the agreement was subject to a successful physical. Skubal’s deal, averaging $50 million annually, is the largest for a pitcher, topping Yoshinobu Yamamoto’s $325 million, 12-year contract with the Los Angeles Dodgers that started in 2024. The previous high for a pitcher’s average salary was $37 million for Jacob deGrom in a $185 million, five-year contract with Texas that began in 2023. Skubal’s agreement includes a full no-trade clause and a $45 million signing bonus that is shielded from the management lockout that threatens the 2027 season, the person said. A two-time All-Star left-hander who turned 30 on Nov. 20, Skubal is 43-17 with a 2.42 ERA in 88 starts over the last four seasons, striking out 655 and walking 95 in 546 innings. Skubal had a $32 million salary this year after winning a record amount in salary arbitration. He was 12-7 with a 2.72 ERA in 26 starts this year for Detroit and the Los Angeles Dodgers, who acquired him on Aug. 2 for three prospects: right-handers River Ryan and Brady Smith, and outfielder Zyhir Hope. Skubal didn’t pitch for the Tigers between April 29 and June 13 because of surgery to remove a loose body in his pitching elbow. Dodgers head team physician Dr. Neal ElAttrache used a NanoNeedle scope 2.0 to perform the procedure, designed to speed recovery. Skubal was 1-1 with a 2.45 ERA in a pair of postseason starts for the Dodgers. He beat Atlanta in a Division Series opener and lost Game 1 of the NL League Championship Series against Milwaukee, allowing two runs over five innings in a 2-1 defeat. The Brewers went on to sweep the two-time defending World Series champions. He averaged 96.8 mph with his four-seam fastball this year, down from 97.6 mph in 2025, when he won his second straight AL Cy Young Award. He threw 38% four-seamers this year, 25.6% changeups, 17.5% sinkers, 13.9% sliders and 5% curveballs. Skubal is 66-44 with a 3.02 ERA in 160 starts and three relief appearances over seven major league seasons with 1,075 strikeouts over 925 1/3 innings.

articles.title: Early Week 12 Fantasy Football Waiver Wire Targets: Cam Ward, Chimere Dike, and 3 Others
articles.summary: The best early targets on the Week 12 waiver wire feature a pair of Titans - Cam Ward and Chimere Dike.
articles.body:
The most locked-in fantasy managers are already looking towards Week 12. We have an ultra-short week of many games, including the Packers-Rams on Wednesday and the usual Thanksgiving Thursday tripleheader. If you want to contend for a league title, you need to dot your I's and cross your T's. I am here to help you all out and list the top early waiver wire targets for this coming Tuesday.

The Titans had been touted as 'hot' offensively, and that continued into Week 11. Despite a 51-30 loss, Ward and company dealt efficiently on offense. Ward threw for 248 yards, 2 touchdowns, and zero interceptions on Sunday. Over his last three games, Ward has thrown for 738 yards, 5 touchdowns, and 1 interception.

Watson will exit the bye week with a gold-medal matchup. The Raiders will make a long trip to Cleveland, where the Browns have the 7th-toughest home field over the last 16 games and the 4th-toughest in the last five seasons.

The Raiders are also allowing the second-most fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks. They have allowed opponents to score at least 30 points in seven of their last eight games.

Running back is spread thin in Week 12, barring any incoming injuries. But if anyone is viable, it is Hill. Over his last four games, Hill has 37 touches for 251 yards and 2 touchdowns. He is also in an elite handcuff situation to Derrick Henry, primed to take over if destiny calls. Other running back handcuff situations aren't as fluid, so it's worth noting this one isn't.

The Packers play on Wednesday, and it increasingly looks like Josh Jacobs will not suit up. That means that Johnson will start. He has 24 rushing attempts, 110 yards, and a touchdown over his last two games.

The Titans have scored 89 points over their last three games. They are heating up, thanks largely to Cam Ward. Dike is also benefiting, as Wan'Dale Robinson is out for the season.

Dike filled the slot role in Week 11, running a 60% slot rate. He caught 6 of 7 targets for 69 yards. He ran seven more routes than Elic Ayomanor and 12 more than Calvin Ridley; he was the team's second-most-used receiver (Carnell Tate).

articles.title: Breaking: Dylan Larkin Traded to Montreal Canadiens for Three-Player Haul
articles.summary: The Detroit Red Wings have finally said enough is enough. Six months after Dylan Larkin requested a trade out of […]
articles.body:
The Detroit Red Wings have finally said enough is enough.

Six months after Dylan Larkin requested a trade out of Detroit, interim general manager Shawn Horcoff has granted the former Red Wings captain's request.

Larkin is going to the Montreal Canadiens alongside a 2028 second-round pick and a 2029 third-round selection from the Red Wings in exchange for goaltender Sam Montembault, forward Kirby Dach, and top prospect center Michael Hage .

Hage is a teammate of current Red Wings prospect JP Hurlbert at the University of Michigan.

Also coming back to Detroit in the trade are conditional first-round picks in 2027 and 2029, a 2027 second-round pick, and a 2028 fourth-rounder.

While the Canadiens were not on Larkin's official 10-team trade list, after losing over a million dollars in the three weeks since deciding he would no longer play for the Red Wings, apparently Detroit was able to convince Larkin to waive his no-trade clause to move north of the border.

Packing his bags for Detroit, meanwhile, Dach has been playing primarily on the Canadiens' third line, with two goals and six assists so far this season while playing on a one-year, $3.6 million contract. Montembault is currently on injured reserve , having last played in March of this year. The 30-year-old veteran netminder has played 232 games in the NHL, primarily with the Canadiens, and is signed to a $3.15 million AAV contract that expires later this year.

DHN will have a story grading the trade posted later.

articles.title: Red Wings trade ex-captain Dylan Larkin to Canadiens in multiplayer and draft-pick deal
articles.summary: The long-awaited trade happened between two Atlantic Division rivals and a month after the Red Wings suspended Larkin without pay.
articles.body:
DETROIT — The Detroit Red Wings traded ex-captain Dylan Larkin to the Montreal Canadiens in a blockbuster swap involving four players and six draft picks, including two first-round selections, in a deal announced by both teams on Sunday night.

In acquiring Larkin, the Red Wings landed forward Kirby Dach, goalie Sam Montembeault and prospect forward Michael Hage as well as Montreal's first-round picks in 2027 and 2029, plus a 2028 second-round selection and a 2028 fourth-rounder.

Along with Larkin, Montreal acquired Detroit's 2028 second-round pick and a third-round selection in 2027.

The long-awaited trade happened between two Atlantic Division rivals and a month after the Red Wings suspended Larkin without pay. The suspension came after the player's agent informed the team the center would no longer play for the franchise, and had grown frustrated by the Red Wings' inability to move him months after he asked to be dealt.

AP Hockey Writer John Wawrow contributed.

articles.title: D Gukesh must step up against Javokhir Sindarov in clash of contrasting chess styles
articles.summary: Whatever may the outcome be, the World Chess Championship between Dommaraju Gukesh and Javokhir Sindarov will be remembered as a unique contest.
articles.body: Whatever may the outcome be, the World Chess Championship between Dommaraju Gukesh and Javokhir Sindarov will be remembered as a unique contest. Both are of almost the same age and the title is being defended by the slightly younger one of the two. For the first time, we are going to see a match between two players so dissimilar to each other in every way.Let me explain after going through the eight games between them. Seeing through the rise of Sindarov is simple - a product of modern Soviet school, with the aggressive Uzbek spice added. Though the Soviet Union disintegrated way back in 1991, the chess expertise of those players was passed on to younger generations. Sindarov grew up with this wisdom and progressed better than the others. He is aggressive, with an excellent sense of initiative and an ability to successfully use it to outplay the opponents.Sindarov developed a good sense of classical chess from the beginning. If I were to compare him with a world champion, I would place him closer to Boris Spassky rather than Botvinnik or Tal – Aggressive, sound, systematic, attacking. Of course, the Challenger doesn’t have the ‘Russian touch’ (command over technique) like Spassky but he has compensated for it with his excellent study of aggressive openings.Gukesh belongs to the ‘Gukesh School of Chess’! He always looked at chess as a battle between two individuals rather than battles between two theories. This has its advantages and disadvantages. He hasn’t developed any prejudices about any positions thereby retaining his originality – but as Magnus Carlsen had put it “when things don’t go his way, he has nothing to fall back on” .When Gukesh and Sindarov played each other for the first time in 2018, the Indian was far behind and the Uzbek clinched the issue quickly in typical Soviet style with black pieces. Thereafter, the players didn’t face each other for another four years until 2022 when Gukesh had already overtaken Sindarov in Elo rating. But lack of knowledge of strategic opening concepts resulted in another dismal loss to the Indian.Strange it may sound, but Gukesh was playing at a much higher level and the next faceoff happened more than two years later when Gukesh was already world champion. In the intervening period, Sindarov was blundering into basic traps like ‘Mate in 1’. Yet, their two games in 2025 were not easy for the world champion. Sindarov had strategically outplayed Gukesh in both these games and the latter had escaped to draws, thanks to his alertness.(The writer is a former seven-time National champion, a GM and FIDE trainer)Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Fed-up Cal Bears fans curse out players after Stanford rout in Big Game
articles.summary: Some Cal football fans have had enough. Following the Golden Bears’ rough 44-28 loss in the “Big Game” to their cross-bay rivals Stanford, falling to 3-8 on...
articles.body:
Following the Golden Bears' rough 44-28 loss in the "Big Game" to their cross-bay rivals Stanford, falling to 3-8 on the season, fans were caught on video cursing out players as they left the field.

It's never good when opposing fans rush the field in your home stadium. But that's not an excuse for fans cussing out college football players and putting it on the internet.

But that's where the Golden Bears find themselves while head coach Tosh Lupoi faces real questions about his job security as an embarrassing season winds down.

But Cal hasn't been competitive for over a month. They haven't won since knocking off Virginia Tech on Oct. 10, and have lost by an average of 26.2 points over their ongoing five-game losing streak. They'll look to snap it in their season finale next week when they host Pittsburgh.

Lupoi signed a five-year, $22.6 million contract that was finalized in early October, meaning moving on would require Cal to take on a hefty buyout while the school faces a serious budget crisis.

Cal's athletic program reportedly came into the season facing a $24 million deficit and laid off some 20 people in the marketing, athletic communications and creative services departments.

All while costs have risen during the transition to the Atlantic Coast Conference following the dismantling of the Pac-12 in 2024.

Suffice to say, barring something drastic and unforeseen, the feeling coming out of Saturday's loss to Stanford won't dissipate anytime soon.

articles.title: Wizards rout the Magic 116-96 to win their 3rd straight following an 8-game skid
articles.summary: WASHINGTON (AP) — Kyshawn George scored 24 points and Anthony Davis added 22 to lead the Washington Wizards to their third straight victory, 116-96 over the...
articles.body:
WASHINGTON (AP) — Kyshawn George scored 24 points and Anthony Davis added 22 to lead the Washington Wizards to their third straight victory, 116-96 over the Orlando Magic on Sunday night.

Trae Young had 11 points and 11 assists for the Wizards, who have rebounded from an early eight-game losing streak. They won with torrid shooting Sunday, going 22 of 39 from 3-point range and never trailing after opening the game with an 11-0 run.

The Wizards have won three in a row for the first time since Feb. 1-5, 2025.

Tristan da Silva scored 18 points and Desmond Bane had 17 for Orlando, which was without star Paolo Banchero because of a sprained ankle.

The Wizards led by as many as 20 in the first half, although it was 63-51 at the break and the Magic quickly cut it to seven in the third quarter. Washington answered with a 12-0 run that included two 3-pointers by George, one by Tre Johnson and another by Young.

A 3 by Bilal Coulibaly made it 97-75 late in the third.

Coulibaly scored 12 points, all on 3s. Johnson had 11 on 4-of-5 shooting. Top overall draft pick AJ Dybantsa scored 16 with eight rebounds and six assists for Washington.

Franz Wagner had 16 points, eight rebounds and six assists for the Magic.

Washington's franchise record for 3-pointers is 23, set in an overtime loss to Indiana on Feb. 12, 2025. Will Riley made what initially looked like the team's 23rd on Sunday, but it was ruled a 2.

articles.title: Jaguars offense gets an F for a sloppy, clunky effort in loss to Giants
articles.summary: Grading the Jacksonville Jaguars 23-18 loss to the New York Giants on Nov. 22.
articles.body:
Grading the Jacksonville Jaguars' 23-18 loss to the New York Giants on Nov. 22 in East Rutherford, N.J.

The Jaguars (7-3) will return home after three road games in a row to host the Tennessee Titans on Nov. 29 at EverBank Stadium.

Jaguars take on Giants at MetLife Stadium. See the photos

Start with nine offensive penalties, including four false starts by four players. There was an illegal formation, an illegal shift, a delay penalty and quarterback Trevor Lawrence came through with an oldie, but never a goodie, throwing a pass beyond the line of scrimmage ... and it wasn't close.

Lawrence had three interceptions if you count the one on a two-point conversion attempt (it's not) and many of his incompletions were high. He was sacked three times and was hit eight other times. The running game struggled because the Giants' defensive line overpowered the Jags offensive line. It was a basic as football gets.

The Jaguars scored only one touchdown in six trips to the red zone against a defense that had given up touchdowns on 80 percent of their oppositions' trips inside the 20-yard line.

What else? How about 5 of 15 on third down (failing to convert on their first seven when it was third-and-eight or longer) and failing to punch the ball in after two shots with 2 yards to go in the third quarter?

This was a borderline 'A' until the Giants' last possession, when the Jags absolutely, positively had to get the ball back with 3:40 left in the game and only one time out left. But J.J. McCarthy hit Malachi Fields for 19 yards and Cam Skattebo ran for two 5-yard gains to give the Giants a first down at the two-minute warning, enabling the victory formation.

Also detracting from the final grade was losing contain on McCarthy, who had a 22-yard scramble on third-and-five and a 13-yard gain on third-and-eight. He had another 29-yard run nullified by a penalty.

Other than that, the Jaguars' defense played well enough to give the offense a chance. The Jaguars failed to score after Antonio Harrison's 42-yard fumble return and a missed 32-yard field goal by Dominic Zvada.

Josh Hines-Allen had his first solo sack since the opening game of the season but McCarthy got hit only three other times. Skattebo was no factor until the final possession (14 carries, 34 yards, 2.4 yards per attempt) and McCarthy threw some terrible passes, with a final rating of 69.3. Malik Nabers got a TD pass but was otherwise invisible and tight end Isaiah Likely caught only one pass. It was a big one, 35 yards, but went for naught when Zavada hooked his field-goal attempt.

For the third game in a row, Cam Little made all four of his field goal attempts, and he's made 18 in a row and 22 of 24 this season. Ameer Abdullah gave the Jaguars great field position with a 47-yard return of the opening kickoff but after getting a first down to the Giants' 14, the offense stalled and Little kicked his first field goal.

The Jags struggled to cover Xavier Gipson on kickoff returns and he had a 27-yard punt return that gave New York prime field position to get Zvada's 51-yard field goal to take a 20-6 halftime lead.

Until the offense was able to finally get some points in the fourth quarter, the Jaguars were failing their first test under the bright lights, in the nation's largest media market, and failing miserably. They had their third game this season with 100 or more yards in penalties, a week after getting called only twice for 20 yards, and otherwise did not seem up to the moment.

They did put together a nice comeback, scoring three times in the fourth quarter, but the defense, which had limited the Giants and McCarthy to 11 yards of offense and 1 for 11 passing on the previous four possessions, let the Giants get the two first downs they needed to run out the clock.

There are always going to be detractors about Coen's thinking when it comes to situational down-and-distance and scoring, and it's the easiest thing in the world to second-guess. But had Coen taken the sure field goal on fourth-and-one at the Giants' 11 in the third quarter, the score is 20-9. Little added another field goal early in the fourth quarter. That makes it 20-12.

Then Brian Thomas Jr.'s touchdown would have made it 20-18 and it's a no-brainer to go for two there. Whether it's made or not, Little kicked his final field goal with 3:40 left, which might have been the game-winner had Coen taken the easy points earlier.

However, Coen has proved, if nothing else, that he's going to roll the dice and not apologize for it. Bottom line is that the Jaguars should have executed on third-and-two and fourth-and-one on the third-quarter possession, and they didn't.

articles.title: Kentucky volleyball sweeps LSU to open SEC Tournament
articles.summary: The Kentucky Wildcats volleyball has advanced in the SEC Tournament thanks to a sweep of LSU on Sunday.
articles.body:
The 2026 SEC Volleyball Tournament is underway, and the Kentucky Wildcats played in their first match on Sunday afternoon. The opened things up with a dominant performance and a sweep of the LSU Tigers 3-0 (25-23, 25-17, 25-19).

LSU got out to an 19-15 lead in the first set, but the Cats roared back with six straight points to take the lead. It was tied at 23 before Kentucky scored the last two points to win the set. Then, they took over, and dominated the final two sets to get the sweep.

Morgan Gaerte was terrific, and led Kentucky with 19 kills and a .432 hit percentage. Brooklyn DeLeye added 14 kills and had just 2 errors. Kassie O'Brien had 44 assists and added a couple of blocks. Molly Tuozzo was everywhere once again, and had 16 digs.

The Wildcats move on to the semifinals of the SEC Tournament now. Their opponent is yet to be determined, but they'll play on Monday night at either 6:00 P.M. or 8:30 P.M. EST.
